Summary: AQUAIVOLT High-Rate AD Simulation incl. CSTR: HRT from 360 h to Hours/Days, 200 Scenarios

BEFORE = conventional mesophilic CSTR, 15-day HRT (360 h), 66.15 m3/d biogas, 151.07 kWh/d. AFTER = 9 pathways: high-rate (H1-H6) and optimized CSTR variants (C1-C3). Research-based - NOT plant measurements.
CSTR physics: in a plain CSTR, SRT = HRT (biomass leaves with effluent), so hours are impossible without washout. C1-C3 cut HRT to 2-7 days instead.
High-rate systems (H1-H3) decouple SRT from HRT via granules or membranes, allowing 4-12 h.

Assumptions: 1. BEFORE = conventional mesophilic CSTR digester at 15-day (360 h) HRT: 66.15 m3/d biogas, 63.63% CH4, 151.07 kWh/d (55,140 kWh/yr). Conventional CSTRs typically need 15-30 days.

2. WHY CSTR CANNOT GO TO HOURS: in a CSTR the contents are fully mixed and biomass leaves with the effluent, so solids retention time equals hydraulic retention time. Methanogens grow slowly (doubling ~1-10 days); at hourly HRT they wash out and the process collapses. That is why CSTR variants (C1-C3) reach 2-7 days, not hours, while granular/membrane systems (H1-H3) reach 4-12 h by retaining biomass.

3. CSTR PATHWAYS: C1 thermophilic CSTR at 55 C - HRT reducible from 15-20 d to ~3 d with stable performance (PMC3811223), thermophilic methanogens grow 2-3x faster; C2 CSTR + NaOH pre-treatment - technical digestion time cut 79.6% and methane +56% (PMC8303515), allowing 4-7 d HRT; C3 hybrid CSTR with fixed-film biomass carriers - partially decouples SRT, 2-4 d HRT (PMC9672170).

4. High-rate anchors: UASB 2-20 h optimal, 4-8 h for high-strength wastewater (SSWM); EGSB +22-32% biogas at fixed OLR (U. Louisville); AnMBR 6-12 h with 70-88% CH4 (PMC8703433); TPAD +50.3% methane (Sci Rep 2024); thermal 50 C pre-treatment +40% methane (PMC10979283). Values above 50% derated to the 40-50% band.
5. AnMBR CH4 70-80%; other technologies 60-68%. Electricity = methane x 3.5892 kWh/m3 (9.97 kWh/m3 x 36% engine efficiency). Gross, before parasitic loads.
6. OLR 4-12 kg COD/m3/d for high-rate (vs ~1-3 conventional); CSTR variants 2-6 kg VS/m3/d. pH 6.9-7.4; H2S 180-260 ppm inlet, 90-95% removed; stability 82-96%.

7. High-rate hourly systems suit soluble COD feeds (wastewater); solid-rich feeds (manure, food waste solids) still need days of hydrolysis - hence TPAD, pre-treatment and CSTR variants keep 48-168 h. Feed type determines technology choice.

8. Research-based planning simulation, NOT plant measurement. Short-HRT performance depends on granulation, membrane fouling control, thermophilic stability and feed characteristics; pilot testing required before investor or grant claims.

Assumptions: 1. BEFORE = conventional mesophilic CSTR digester at 15-day (360 h) HRT, matching the Aquaivolt baseline production of 66.15 m3/d biogas, 63.63% CH4, 151.07 kWh/d (55,140 kWh/yr). Conventional digesters typically need 20-30 days.

2. AFTER = advanced high-rate anaerobic technologies operating at HRT of hours: UASB 4-12 h (optimal 2-20 h per SSWM; 4-8 h for high-strength wastewater); EGSB 4-10 h; AnMBR 6-12 h (membrane retention); TPAD 48-96 h (thermophilic 55 C + mesophilic 35 C phases); pre-treatment routes 24-72 h.

3. Key scientific principle: high-rate systems decouple hydraulic retention (hours) from solids retention (12-60 days) via granular sludge (UASB/EGSB) or membranes (AnMBR). Biomass stays in the reactor while liquid passes through quickly. TPAD accelerates hydrolysis thermophilically: thermophilic methanogens grow 2-3x faster than mesophilic.

4. Biogas increase +40% to +50% is anchored to published results: TPAD +50.3% methane vs mesophilic (Sci Rep 2024, s41598-024-62998-w); TPAD +26-60% vs single stage (Chem Eng J 2015); thermochemical NaOH +56% methane and -79.6% technical digestion time (Molecules 2021, PMC8303515); thermal pre-treatment 50 C +40% methane (PMC10979283); EGSB +22-32% biogas rate at fixed OLR (Univ. Louisville ETD). Values above 50% were derated to the 40-50% band.

5. AnMBR scenarios use CH4 70-80% (literature: 70-88% methane in AnMBR biogas); other technologies 60-68%. Electricity = methane x 3.5892 kWh/m3 (9.97 kWh/m3 x 36% engine efficiency). Gross, before parasitic loads.

6. OLR 4-12 kg COD/m3/d for high-rate systems (vs ~1-3 for conventional); upflow velocity 0.5-2 m/h (UASB) and 4-8 m/h (EGSB); pH 6.9-7.4; H2S 180-260 ppm inlet, 90-95% removed; stability index 82-96%.

7. IMPORTANT: high-rate systems apply to soluble/wastewater-type feeds (COD basis). For solid-rich substrates (slurry, manure, food waste solids), particle hydrolysis still needs days - hence TPAD and pre-treatment pathways retain 24-96 h rather than 4-12 h. Selecting a technology requires knowing the feed type.

8. This is a research-based planning simulation, NOT plant measurement and NOT a validated model of a specific reactor. Short-HRT performance depends on biomass granulation, membrane fouling control and feed characteristics; pilot testing at the Aquaivolt site is required before investor or grant claims.
